raw_case_text:
A 31-year-old male with ESKD secondary to IgA nephropathy received a deceased donor kidney transplant four years prior to presentation. Antibody-mediated rejection (ABMR) was diagnosed on the basis of typical changes on light microscopy (including peritubular capillaritis) and positive staining for C4d staining and the presence in the serum of new donor specific antibodies. The patient was on maintenance immunosuppression consisting of tacrolimus 1.5 mg twice daily, mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg twice daily, and prednisolone 5 mg once daily. He denied noncompliance and had acceptable immunosuppressant drug trough levels.
The patient received 250 mg methylprednisolone daily for three days and underwent five sessions of plasma exchange followed by IVIG (1 g/kg) at a slow rate of 54 ml/hour increasing to 108 ml/hour as per protocol with concomitant IV normal saline and paracetamol, prophylactic cotrimoxazole, and valacyclovir. The total dose received was 90 g. Less than 24 hours after the final dose of IVIG, he presented to emergency services with a severe headache, photophobia, and nuchal rigidity. He had no other neurological symptoms or signs.
Computerized tomography (CT) neuroimaging was noncontributory. Lumbar punctures on days 1 and 2 of admission yielded clear cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with a polymorphic leukocytosis, elevated protein, and low glucose (Table 1). Gram stain and culture were negative. Serum C-reactive protein and white cell count were normal.
Broad-spectrum empiric antimicrobial therapy was started at presentation. This consisted of high dose intravenous acyclovir, vancomycin, cefotaxime, and amoxicillin.
Microbiological analysis of CSF samples was negative for culture and PCR of typical and atypical bacterial and viral causes of meningitis, as described below.
CSF samples were negative for the following: Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Cryptococcus neoformans, Listeria monocytogenes, cytomegalovirus (CMV), enterovirus, Herpes simplex virus, and Varicella zoster virus as well as acid fast bacilli (Table 2). Serum testing for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C was also negative (Table 3).
As microbiological tests were negative, initial empirical antimicrobials were discontinued by day seven of admission and the patient was managed supportively with intravenous fluids, analgesia, and antiemetics. IVIG treatment had been completed prior to this presentation and the patient did not require further doses. By day five, the patient was asymptomatic. Four weeks after discharge the patient remained well and was continued on a higher dose of maintenance immunosuppression during this time, with stable graft function.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 31-year-old male kidney transplant recipient presented with severe headache, photophobia, and nuchal rigidity less than 24 hours after completing high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, who had undergone deceased-donor kidney transplantation 4 years prior for IgA nephropathy, was treated for biopsy-proven C4d-positive antibody-mediated rejection with 3 days of IV methylprednisolone (250 mg/day), 5 sessions of plasma exchange, and high-dose IVIG (1 g/kg, total 90 g infused at 54-108 mL/h). Less than 24 hours after the final IVIG infusion, he presented to the emergency department with acute severe headache, photophobia, and neck stiffness.
subjective.past_medical_history: End-stage kidney disease secondary to IgA nephropathy status post deceased-donor renal transplantation 4 years prior, complicated by acute antibody-mediated rejection.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for severe headache, photophobia, and neck stiffness. Negative for focal neurological symptoms. Home/recent medications: tacrolimus 1.5 mg twice daily, mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg twice daily, prednisolone 5 mg daily, cotrimoxazole, valacyclovir, methylprednisolone, and IVIG (90 g).

objective.physical_examination: Nuchal rigidity and photophobia without focal neurological deficits.
objective.routine_investigations: Serum CRP and peripheral WBC count were normal; serum testing for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C was negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Head CT was noncontributory. Lumbar punctures on hospital days 1 and 2 yielded clear CSF with polymorphonuclear leukocytosis, elevated protein, and low glucose, but negative Gram stain, negative bacterial/fungal/mycobacterial cultures, and negative CSF PCR/antigen testing for Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Cryptococcus neoformans, Listeria monocytogenes, CMV, enterovirus, HSV, VZV, and acid-fast bacilli.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)-induced aseptic meningitis in a renal transplant recipient, established after CSF cultures and PCR/antigen panels ruled out bacterial, viral, mycobacterial, and Cryptococcus neoformans meningitis. Empirical IV acyclovir, vancomycin, cefotaxime, and amoxicillin were discontinued on day 7; with supportive care (IV fluids, analgesics, antiemetics), the patient became completely asymptomatic by day 5 and remained well with stable graft function at 4-week follow-up.
